title: Speed bundle: pearl targeting gathers its diamond ring by ring and stops early, one-pass parser, cheaper whole-map passes on first turns, PROTOCOL 3 only when needed
hypothesis: Measured 2026-09-27 on champion 38046fa by replaying 1,086 recorded bot processes (default and big_empty, seed 12345) in the toolkit's metered sandbox (per-turn points equal the game's on 21,514 of 21,514 non-first turns). A p50 turn is 3.75M points, of which the one output flush is about 3.0M (2.5M + 4,000/byte, 105-130 bytes), so compute is ~0.8-0.9M and a 5% p50 cut needs ~25% less compute. Compute on big_empty: pearl targeting 33% (scanning 421 tiles a turn 20%), move scoring 19%, parsing 17.5%, symmetry 12%, gossip 6.5%. p99 on big maps is set by split children's first turns (world setup 579K, whole-map explore search ~1M, symmetry rewrite 1.69M on 454 turns). Changes, each keeping the same candidates, order and ties: (1) choosePearl gathers the radius-14 diamond ring by ring (fast tiles first) and stops once no farther ring can win (needs every penalty non-negative: static_assert), same 24-candidate cap; each tile once at its shortest torus offset; (2) gossip ranks small keys and builds only the 4 kept Records; (3) scanRegion as a bit-row BFS via openRow/jumpSides, old BFS when any unknown-portal side exists; (4) symmetry's full rewrite visits only tiles seen or next to seen (skipped ones were no-ops); (5) parser fast paths for tile, edge and body lines in one pass, reusing the 49 Tile slots; (6) send PROTOCOL 3 only when the input lacked ECHOES (unverified that the engine keeps protocol 3 once asked; if not, drop this part); (7) edgeOf from a table filled in init's existing loop; (8) memset in World/Belief init. A prototype of all eight is at ~/.bc-loop/research/speed-bundle-38046fa.patch (814 lines; the orchestrator can paste parts on request, since the lane can't read ~/.bc-loop). Measured on the prototype: p50 -5.1% default, -6.6% big_empty; p99 -2.9% / -15.9%; stdout identical on 1,086 of 1,086 processes. Without (6), about -3.9% / -5.5%, under the gate. Narrow maps (under 29 tiles a side, most ladder maps) should gain more from (1) but are unmeasured. test_protocol.py assumes PROTOCOL 3 every turn and needs updating; test_speed's gatherCandidates check no longer covers choosePearl. Value is small: the champion's p99 is 5.8M against the judge's 50M limit, and the bot's own compute is ~23% of a native test game's CPU (one profiled game), so this buys ~1% more test games; hence priority 4.
